# requireSheet

<link-summary>Returns the value as a sheet, or throws.</link-summary>

<web-summary>requireSheet() — Returns the value as a sheet, or throws. apps-script-utils, English.</web-summary>

<tldr>
<p>Module: <code>appsscript/sheet</code> · Since: 1.5.0</p>
</tldr>

```typescript
function requireSheet(value: unknown, message?: string): GoogleAppsScript.Spreadsheet.Sheet;
```

An Apps Script service object has no constructor a script can test against, so the guard reads the tag the object reports for itself: `value.toString() === "Sheet"`. A plain object that reports the same tag passes too, which in practice means a test double.

`isX` and `nonX` answer a question and never interrupt control flow; `requireX` and `requireNonX` hand the value back or throw. The scheme is explained in [](validation-conventions.md).

## Parameters

| Parameter              | Type      | Description                                                   |
| :--------------------- | :-------- | :------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `value`                | `unknown` | The value to validate.                                        |
| `message` _(optional)_ | `string`  | The message of the exception. A default is used when omitted. |

## Returns

`GoogleAppsScript.Spreadsheet.Sheet` — the same value, typed as a sheet.

## Throws

| Exception               | Condition                 |
| :---------------------- | :------------------------ |
| `InvalidSheetException` | the value is not a sheet. |

## Examples

### What passes and what does not

```javascript
const sheet = SpreadsheetApp.getActiveSheet();

requireSheet(sheet); // => sheet
requireSheet({}); // throws InvalidSheetException
requireSheet(null); // throws InvalidSheetException
```
